entries.tamil_text: அகர முதல எழுத்தெல்லாம் ஆதி பகவன் முதற்றே உலகு
entries.meaning: As the letter 'A' is the first of all letters, so the eternal God is first in the world.
entries.context: This is the opening verse of Thirukkural. Just as every letter in the Tamil alphabet follows from 'A', everything in existence originates from and depends on the eternal, beginningless God.
entries.author: Thiruvalluvar

entries.tamil_text: கற்றதனால் ஆய பயனென்கொல் வாலறிவன் நற்றாள் தொழாஅர் எனின்
entries.meaning: What is the use of learning, if one does not worship the good feet of Him who possesses pure knowledge?
entries.context: This verse teaches that all worldly learning is meaningless unless it leads a person toward devotion to the divine and pure wisdom.
entries.author: Thiruvalluvar

entries.tamil_text: மலர்மிசை ஏகினான் மாணடி சேர்ந்தார் நிலமிசை நீடு வாழ்வார்
entries.meaning: Those who reach the glorious feet of the One who dwells upon the flower (the lotus of the heart) will live long and gloriously on this earth.
entries.context: This verse says that devotion to God, who resides in the heart like a lotus, brings a life of lasting honor and fulfillment.
entries.author: Thiruvalluvar

entries.tamil_text: வேண்டுதல் வேண்டாமை இலான் அடிசேர்ந்தார்க்கு யாண்டும் இடும்பை இல
entries.meaning: Those who reach the feet of the One who is free from desire and aversion will never face sorrow, at any time.
entries.context: This verse explains that God is perfect and complete, having no wants or dislikes, and those devoted to such a God are freed from life's distresses.
entries.author: Thiruvalluvar

entries.tamil_text: இருள்சேர் இருவினையும் சேரா இறைவன் பொருள்சேர் புகழ்புரிந்தார் மாட்டு
entries.meaning: Neither of the two kinds of deeds (good or bad), which are tainted with darkness, will touch those who have truly praised the worthy glory of God.
entries.context: This verse teaches that both meritorious and demeritorious deeds keep one bound to worldly cycles, but true devotion to God rises above both, leading to liberation.
entries.author: Thiruvalluvar

entries.tamil_text: பொறிவாயில் ஐந்தவித்தான் பொய்தீர் ஒழுக்க நெறிநின்றார் நீடு வாழ்வார்
entries.meaning: Those who follow the truthful path of the One who has conquered the five senses will live long and prosper.
entries.context: This verse praises God as having mastered the five sense-gates, and says that following that same truthful, disciplined path leads to a flourishing life.
entries.author: Thiruvalluvar

entries.tamil_text: தனக்குவமை இல்லாதான் தாள்சேர்ந்தார்க்கு அல்லால் மனக்கவலை மாற்றல் அரிது
entries.meaning: Except for those who have reached the feet of the One who has no comparison, it is difficult for anyone else to remove the anxieties of the mind.
entries.context: This verse states that true peace of mind, freeing oneself from worry, is only possible through devotion to the incomparable, supreme God.
entries.author: Thiruvalluvar

entries.tamil_text: அறவாழி அந்தணன் தாள்சேர்ந்தார்க்கு அல்லால் பிறவாழி நீந்தல் அரிது
entries.meaning: Except for those who reach the feet of the compassionate One who is an ocean of righteousness, it is difficult to swim across the other ocean, the ocean of births (the cycle of rebirth).
entries.context: This verse uses the metaphor of two oceans: God's ocean of righteousness, and the ocean of endless birth and rebirth. Only through devotion can one cross the latter.
entries.author: Thiruvalluvar

entries.tamil_text: கோளில் பொறியில் குணமிலவே எண்குணத்தான் தாளை வணங்காத் தலை
entries.meaning: A head that does not bow to the feet of the One possessing the eight great qualities is as useless as a sense organ that has lost its function.
entries.context: This verse compares a person who does not show devotion to God to a malfunctioning organ — technically present but serving no true purpose.
entries.author: Thiruvalluvar

entries.tamil_text: பிறவிப் பெருங்கடல் நீந்துவர் நீந்தார் இறைவன் அடி சேராதார்
entries.meaning: Those who reach the feet of God will swim across the great ocean of births; those who do not reach His feet will not.
entries.context: This closing verse of the first chapter reinforces that liberation from the endless cycle of birth and rebirth comes only through devotion to God.
entries.author: Thiruvalluvar
